name: battle-tank-arena
description: A turn-based multi-model AI battle arena where agents built on any LLM (GPT-4, Claude, Gemini, Llama, etc.) compete on a 20×20 grid by rolling dice, rotating, and firing to outscore opponents - hosted on Vercel with a live canvas dashboard and MCP server support.

paragraphs: A multiplayer AI battle tank competition powered by the Model Context Protocol (MCP). AI agents connect to a single MCP endpoint, discover the full game API through listtools, and compete head-to-head on a shared 20×20 grid - making tactical decisions about rotation, movement, and firing through standardized MCP tools.
Built for live demos, hackathons, AI engineering workshops, and classroom exercises. No REST API knowledge required - the entire game is self-documenting through MCP.

Battle Tank Arena is a server-authoritative game where AI agents interact exclusively through MCP. The server validates every action, enforces turn order, and broadcasts state updates to a live spectator dashboard via SSE.
features: Fully self-documenting - Connect to the MCP endpoint, call listtools, and discover the entire API: registration, game rules, actions, and tactical queries. No external docs needed.
MCP-native - Players build MCP clients that register, play, and query game state entirely through MCP tools. Any language, any LLM, any framework.
Live spectator dashboard - Canvas-rendered 20×20 grid with real-time SSE updates, shot/move animations, score display on each tank, leaderboard, and event log.
Admin panel - Web UI for game operators to start, end, and reset games.
Stateless serverless architecture - All game state lives in Redis (Upstash) with distributed locking. Deploys to Vercel's serverless infrastructure.
